name: Reticulate Acropigmentation of Kitamura

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Reticulate Acropigmentation of Kitamura

criteria.description: Presence of reticulate hyperpigmented macules primarily on the dorsal aspects of hands and feet
Characteristic pitted or atrophic scars on the palmar surfaces
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Onset of pigmentation during childhood or adolescence

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of reticulate hyperpigmentation on acral areas plus pitted palmar scars
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ADAM10 mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reticulate hyperpigmented macules on dorsal hands and feet
searchTerms: net-like dark spots on back of hands and feet
lace-patterned dark skin on hands and feet
small pitted or sunken scars on palms

common.symptomName: Progressive extension of pigmentation to forearms and lower legs
searchTerms: pigmentation spreading to forearms and lower legs
dark skin patches extending on limbs
progressive skin darkening on arms and legs

common.symptomName: Fine linear hyperpigmentation on the dorsal fingers
searchTerms: fine linear dark streaks on back of fingers
thin pigmented lines on dorsal fingers

common.symptomName: Mild hypopigmented macules interspersed within hyperpigmented areas
searchTerms: small light spots mixed with dark patches
mild hypopigmented macules within pigmented areas
light skin spots among darker skin
mild thickening of skin on palms and soles
rough skin on hands and feet
slight thinning of skin on fingers and toes
abnormal dark or light spots on mucous membranes
pigmentation changes inside mouth or nose

rare.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to pigmented areas
searchTerms: mild itching in pigmented skin areas
mild excessive sweating on palms and soles
increased sweating on hands and feet

other: Histopathology showing epidermal atrophy with increased basal layer pigmentation and melanophages in the dermis

distinguishingFeatures: Flexural reticulate hyperpigmentation rather than acral distribution
Presence of comedo-like lesions and pitted scars on the face
Hypopigmented macules mixed with hyperpigmented macules on the dorsal hands and feet
Onset in infancy or early childhood

redFlags: Rapid progression of pigmentation beyond acral areas
Development of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Presence of ulceration or nodular skin lesions
references: Kitamura K. Reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura. J Dermatol. 1976;3(1):1-7.
Hamada T, et al. ADAM10 mutations cause reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura. Nat Genet. 2016;48(1):101-105.
